notes.2389: (tn): This word, דְּאָבָה (d�’avah) is a hapax legomenon. But the verbal root means “to languish; to pine.” A related noun talks of dejection and despair in Deut 28:65. So here “despair” as a translation is preferable to “terror.”

rashi.heb:
*תחתיו חדודי חרש.* 
במקום חניתו יש זהרורי שמש כי סנפירים שלו אשר תחתיו בבטנו מאירות ומזריחות כשמש:
rashi.eng: *Under him are rays of the sun.* in the place he rests, there are rays of the sun, because his fins, which are under him on his belly, illuminate and shine like the sun.

rashi.heb:
*חדודי.* 
כמו חרב חדה שהיא שנונה צחה ומלובנה וע"ש כך קורא לזהרורי חדודי:
rashi.eng: *rays.* Heb. חדודי, like a sharp sword, which is sharpened, bright, and whitened. Because of this, he calls rays חַדוּדֵי.

rashi.heb:
*חרש.* 
שמש כמו האומר לחרס לא יזרח וגו' (לעיל ט) בטרם תבא החרס' (שופטים י״ד:י״ח):
rashi.eng: *sun.* Heb. חרשׂ, the sun, like (above 9:7), “He who spoke to the sun (לחרס) and it did not shine;” (Jud. 14:18); “before the sun (החרסה) set. ”

rashi.heb:
*ירפד חרוץ עלי טיט.* 
מלה כפולה ירפד חרוץ מוסב על חדודי חרס עלי טיט מוסב על תחתיתו במקום שהוא שם על החול זה טיט ריפודו מזריח כזהב חרוץ כעניין שנא' רפידתו זהב (שיר ג) חרוץ מין זהב כעניין שנא' מחרוץ תבואתה (משלי ג) טוב פריה מחרוץ ומפז (שם ח), ירפד ל' מצע ומשכב כמו רפידתו זהב (שיר ג):
rashi.eng: *where he lies is gold upon the mire.* This is a repeated clause. “Where he lies is gold,” refers to “rays of the sun;” “upon the mire” refers to “under him,” in the place where he is on the sand; this is the mire where he lies. It shines like precious gold, as it is stated (Song 3:10): “its couch of gold.” חָרוּץ is a type of gold, as it is stated (Prov. 8:19): “My fruit is better than gold (מחרוץ), yea than fine gold.” Where he lies-an expression of a couch for lying down, like (Song 3:10), “its couch (רפידתו) of gold.”

notes.2391: (tn): The last clause says “it cannot be moved.” But this part will function adverbially in the sentence.

rashi.heb:
*ירתיח כסיר מצולה.* 
כסיר קטן נפוח שמעל' מהרה רתיחו' תכופות ורצופות כן הוא מרתיח את המצולה שהיא גדול' ועמוק':
rashi.eng: *He makes the deep seethe like a pot.* Like a small bubbling pot, that quickly raises bubbles one after another, so does he cause the deep, which is large and deep, to seethe.

rashi.heb:
*ים ישים כמרקחה.* 
כמרקחת ריקוח בשמים שהיא מעורה ומעורבת כמו כן ישים ויערב את הים כשהוא זז ממקומו:
rashi.eng: *he makes the sea like a seething mixture.* Like a mixture of a concoction of spices, which is compounded and mixed, so does he make and mix the sea when he moves from his place.

notes.2392: (tn): The description of his heart being “hard” means that he is cruel and fearless. The word for “hard” is the word encountered before for molten or cast metal.

rashi.heb:
*אחריו יאיר נתיב.* 
כשהוא פורח ושט בים אחריו מאיר נתיב התהום שלפי שעה שהוא פורח ואין שם מים מחמת מרוצת פריחתו:
rashi.eng: *He makes a path shine after him.* When he swims and floats in the sea, he makes the path of the deep shine, for at the time he swims, there is no water because of the speed of his swimming.

rashi.heb:
*יחשוב תהום לשיבה.* 
תהום חשוב לפניו בחלשות ותשות:
rashi.eng: *he considers the deep to be hoary.* To him, the deep is considered to be weak and feeble.

rashi.heb:
*לשיבה.* 
לחלשות של זקנה ושיבה:
rashi.eng: *to be hoary.* The weakness of old age and hoariness.

notes.2393: (tc): This verse has created all kinds of problems for the commentators. The first part is workable: “when he raises himself up, the mighty [the gods] are terrified.” The mythological approach would render אֵלִים (’elim) as “gods.” But the last two words, which could be rendered “at the breaking [crashing, or breakers] they fail,” receive much attention. E. Dhorme (Job, 639) suggests “majesty” for “raising up” and “billows” (גַּלִּים, gallim) for אֵלִים (’elim), and gets a better parallelism: “the billows are afraid of his majesty, and the waves draw back.” But H. H. Rowley (Job [NCBC], 263) does not think this is relevant to the context, which is talking about the creature’s defense against attack. The RSV works well for the first part, but the second part need some change; so Rowley adopts “in their dire consternation they are beside themselves.”

rashi.heb:
*אין על עפר משלו.* 
מ"ם חטף קמץ ופתרונו ממשלתו שאין בריה מושלת עליו והוא שם דבר מושל ושלטון וע"כ המ"ם מנוקדת בחטף קמ"ץ:
rashi.eng: *On the dust there is none that rules over him.* The “mem ” [is vowelized] with a “hataf kamatz,” and it means his rule, that no creature rules over him, and it is a noun denoting a ruler. Therefore, the “mem” is vowelized with a “hataf kamatz.”

rashi.heb:
*העשו.* 
כמו העשוי ולא ידעתי לו ריע ופתרונו העשוי בלי פחד ומחיתה שאינו מתיירא מן הבריות כמו שנאמר בסוס ישחק לפחד ולא ייחת (לעיל לט):
rashi.eng: *which is made.* Heb. העשו, like העשוי [the passive participle]. However, I know of no similar case [in Scripture]. It means one that was made without fear or dismay, that is not afraid of the creatures, as it is stated concerning the horse (above 39:22): “He scorns fear and is not dismayed.”

notes.2394: (tn): This is the clearest reading, following A. B. Davidson, Job, 285. The versions took different readings of the construction.
notes.2395: (tn): The verb קוּם (qum, “stand”) with בְּלִי (b�li, “not”) has the sense of “does not hold firm,” or “gives way.”

rashi.heb:
*את כל גבוה יראה.* 
כל הגבוהים שבעולם הוא רואה תחתיו וכן הוא מנהג העול' אשר אותו העומד למעלה רואה את התחתון יותר ממה שרואה התחתון ואין לתחתון גבורה ונצחון נגד העליון ולויתן זה רואה את כל הגבורים לומר שאין להם גבורה כנגדו:
rashi.eng: *He looks at all high things.* All the high things in the world he sees beneath himself, for so is the custom of the world, that whoever stands above sees the one below more than the one below sees [him]. Also, the one below has no power or victory against the one above. Now this leviathan sees all mighty men; that is to say, they have no power against him.

rashi.heb:
*הוא מלך על כל בני שחץ.* 
מלה כפולה על כל גאוה יראה והוא מלך על כל בני שחץ בני גסות הרוח שבראתי בעולמי שאין להם כנגדו ממשלה ושרר' והאיך נשאך לבך לשאת ראש לפני להתוכח נגדי כי הנני עושה את כל הנפלאות האלה:
rashi.eng: *he is king over all proud beasts.* This is a repeated expression. He looks over all proud beasts and he is king over all the proud beasts, over all haughty creatures that I created in My world, who have no rule or dominion against him. Now how did you dare to lift your head before Me, since I perform all these wonders?

notes.2397: (tn): The verb is plural, but since there is no expressed subject it is translated as a passive here.

notes.2399: (tn): Here only the word “sharp” is present, but in passages like Isa 41:15 it is joined with “threshing sledge.” Here and in Amos 1:3 and Isa 28:27 the word stands alone, but represents the “sledge.”

notes.2400: (sn): The idea is either that the sea is stirred up like the foam from beating the ingredients together, or it is the musk-smell that is the point of comparison.

notes.2402: (tn, Heb): “the sons of pride.” Dhorme repoints the last word to get “all the wild beasts,” but this misses the point of the verse. This animal looks over every proud creature – but he is king of them all in that department.

rashi.heb:
*ידעתי כי כל תוכל.* 
כי הכל תוכל לעשות כאשר ישר בעיניך:
rashi.eng: *I knew that You can do everything.* That You can do anything that pleases You.

rashi.heb:
*ולא יבצר ממך מזמה.* 
כופל מלתו שאין מזמה ומחשבה נבצרת ונסתרת ממך אשר כל מחשבותיך תוכל לגמור ולמלאות כי בידך כח וגבורה ובידך לעשות כל הטוב בעיניך ומקרא זה דוגמת ועתה לא יבצר מהם כל אשר יזמו לעשות (בראשית י״א:ו׳):
rashi.eng: *and no design is restrained from You.* He repeats his words, that no design or plan is restrained or withheld from You, that You can complete and fulfill Your plans, for strength and might are in Your hand, and You have the power to do all that pleases You. This verse is similar to (Gen. 11:6), “Now will nothing that they have planned to do be restrained (יבצר) from them?”

notes.2403: (tn): The expression “you asked” is added here to clarify the presence of the line to follow. Many commentators delete it as a gloss from Job 38:2. If it is retained, then Job has to be recalling God’s question before he answers it.
notes.2404: (tn): The word לָכֵן (lakhen) is simply “but,” as in Job 31:37.
notes.2405: (tn, Heb): “and I do not understand.” The expression serves here in an adverbial capacity. It also could be subordinated as a complement: “I have declared [things that] I do not understand.”
notes.2406: (tn): The last clause is “and I do not know.” This is also subordinated to become a dependent clause.

rashi.heb:
*מי זה מעלים.* 
אשר העלים וכסה עצתו ונפלאותיו של הקב"ה בבלי דעת, ידעתי כי הכל בידך לעשות וע"כ הגדתי קצת מגבורותיו כאשר היו עם לבבי כאש' ידעתי:
rashi.eng: *Who is this.* who concealed and covered the counsel and the wonders of the Holy One, blessed be He, without knowledge? I knew that everything is in Your hand to do, and so I related some of Your mighty deeds as were in my heart; as I knew [them].

rashi.heb:
*ולא אבין.* 
אבל לא הבנתי כ"כ כאשר הודעתני כי כמה נפלאות נסתרות ונעלמות ממני אשר אינני יודע:
rashi.eng: *but I did not understand.* But I did not understand so much, as You informed me, for many wonders are hidden and concealed from me, which I do not know.

notes.2407: (tn): This phrase, “you said,” is supplied in the translation to introduce the recollection of God’s words.

notes.2408: (sn): This statement does not imply there was a vision. He is simply saying that this experience of God was real and personal. In the past his knowledge of God was what he had heard – hearsay. This was real.

rashi.heb:
*לשמע אוזן שמעתיך.* 
כמה וכמה פעמים שמעתי שמעך:
rashi.eng: *I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear.* Many many times I have heard of You.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה עיני ראתה.* 
את שכינתך:
rashi.eng: *and now, my eye has seen You.* Your Shechinah.

notes.2409: (tn): Or “despise what I said.” There is no object on the verb; Job could be despising himself or the things he said (see L. J. Kuyper, “Repentance of Job,” VT 9 [1959]: 91-94).

rashi.heb:
*על כן.* 
אשר זכיתי לחזות שכינתך:
rashi.eng: *Therefore.* Since I merited to see Your Shechinah.

rashi.heb:
*אמאס.* 
מואס אני בחיי:
rashi.eng: *I despise.* I despise my life.

rashi.heb:
*על עפר ואפר.* 
ואהיה מתנחם אילו הייתי שוכן בקבר לשוב לעפר ואפר אשר לוקחתי משם:
rashi.eng: *on dust and ashes.* if I were resting in the grave, to return to dust and ashes whence I was taken.

notes.2410: (tn, Heb): “the Lord.” The title has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.2412: (tn): The form נְכוֹנָה (n�khonah) is from כּוּן (kun, “to be firm; to be fixed; to be established”). Here it means “the right thing” or “truth.” The Akkadian word kenu (from כּוּן, kun) connotes justice and truth.

rashi.heb:
*ובשני רעיך.* 
בלדד השוחי וצופר הנעמתי:
rashi.eng: *and your two companions.* Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite.

rashi.heb:
*כי לא דברתם.* 
שהרי לא דברתם אלי טענה נכונה כעבדי איוב שהרי הוא לא פשע בי כי אם על אשר אמר (לעיל ט) תם ורשע הוא מכלה וע"י השטן המקטרג את העולם שנאמר (שם) אם שוט ימית פתאום וגו' ואם הוסיף לדבר מפני קושי יסורין אשר כבדו וחזקו עליו דבר אבל אתם פשעתם על אשר הרשעתם אותו לאמר (לעיל ד) הלא יראתך כסלתך והתחזקתם אותו בחזקת רשע ולבסוף הייתם משותקים ומנוצחים לפניו והיה לכם לנחמו כאשר עשה אליהוא ולא די לאיוב בצרתו ויסוריו כי גם הוספתם על חטאתיכם פשע להקניטו:
rashi.eng: *because you did not speak.* Because you did not speak to Me with a correct argument as did My servant Job, for he did not rebel against Me except for what he said (above 9:22), “He destroys both the innocent and the wicked,” and through the Adversary who denounces the world, as it is stated (ibid. verse 23): “If the scourge kills suddenly etc.” And if he continued to speak, he spoke because of the severity of the pains that burdened him and overwhelmed him; but you rebelled by condemning him, saying (4:6), “Behold, your fear was your foolishness,” and you held him to be a wicked man, and at the end when you were silenced and defeated before him, you should have consoled him as Elihu did. Was it not enough for Job with his trouble and his sufferings, that you added rebellion to your sins to provoke him?

notes.2413: (tn): The imperatives in this verse are plural, so all three had to do this together.
notes.2414: (tn): The verb “pray” is the Hitpael from the root פָּלַל (palal). That root has the main idea of arbitration; so in this stem it means “to seek arbitration [for oneself],” or “to pray,” or “to intercede.”
notes.2415: (tn, Heb): “I will lift up his face,” meaning, “I will regard him.”
notes.2416: (tn): This clause is a result clause, using the negated infinitive construct.
notes.2417: (tn): The word “folly” can also be taken in the sense of “disgrace.” If the latter is chosen, the word serves as the direct object. If the former, then it is an adverbial accusative.
notes.2418: (sn): The difference between what they said and what Job said, therefore, has to do with truth. Job was honest, spoke the truth, poured out his complaints, but never blasphemed God. For his words God said he told the truth. He did so with incomplete understanding, and with all the impatience and frustration one might expect. Now the friends, however, did not tell what was right about God. They were not honest; rather, they were self-righteous and condescending. They were saying what they thought should be said, but it was wrong.

rashi.heb:
*והעליתם עולה בעדכם.* 
למען שתתרצו ותתפייסו לפני ובלבד אשר עבדי איוב יתפלל עליכם אשר אסלח לחטאתיכם ולפשעיכם לא אזכר עוד:
rashi.eng: *and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves.* So that you placate and appease Me, provided that My servant Job pray for you that I forgive your sins, and no longer remember your transgressions.

rashi.heb:
*כי אם פניו אשא.* 
שהרי פניו אשא לקבל תפלתו הרי אם כמו אשר וכן עד אם כלו לשתות (בראשית כ״ד:י״ט) אם כופר יושת עליו (שמות כ״א:ל׳) וכן הרבה:
rashi.eng: *for I will favor him.* Heb. כי אם, because I will favor him to accept his prayer (thus the word אִם is used for “that”), and likewise (Gen. 24:19), “until (עד אם) they have finished drinking;” (Ex. 21:30), “in which case (אם) an atonement is placed on him,” and many others.

rashi.heb:
*כי לא.* 
שהרי לא:
rashi.eng: *for… not.* Because… not.

notes.2419: (tn): The expression “had respect for Job” means God answered his prayer.

rashi.heb:
*וישא ה' את פני איוב.* 
וישא כמו נשאתי פניך גם לדבר הזה (ראשית יט) שקבל תפלתו והסביר לו פנים:
rashi.eng: *and the Lord favored Job.* Heb. וישא, [lit. and the Lord lifted His countenance] as in (Gen. 19:21), “I have favored you (נשאתי) also in this respect,” that He accepted his prayer and showed him a bright countenance.

notes.2420: (tn): The paragraph begins with the disjunctive vav, “Now as for the Lord, he….”
notes.2421: (sn): The expression here is interesting: “he returned the captivity of Job,” a clause used elsewhere in the Bible of Israel (see e.g., Ps 126). Here it must mean “the fortunes of Job,” i.e., what he had lost. There is a good deal of literature on this; for example, see R. Borger, “Zu sub sb(i)t,” ZAW 25 (1954): 315-16; and E. Baumann, ZAW 6 (1929): 17ff.
notes.2422: (tn): This is a temporal clause, using the infinitive construct with the subject genitive suffix. By this it seems that this act of Job was also something of a prerequisite for restoration – to pray for them.
notes.2423: (tn): The construction uses the verb “and he added” with the word “repeat” (or “twice”).

rashi.heb:
*שב את שבות.* 
איוב בהתפללו שב נופל לומר בענין זה והרי הוא כאילו כתיב והשיב את שבות איוב:
rashi.eng: *Now the Lord returned Job’s captivity when he prayed.* [The word] שָׁב is inappropriate in this matter, and it is as though it were written: “And He returned (נשאתי) Job’s captivity when he prayed.”

rashi.heb:
*בהתפללו בעד רעהו.* 
בזכות שהתפלל על כל ריע וריע שלו:
rashi.eng: *for his friend.* In the merit that he prayed for each friend of his.

rashi.heb:
*למשנה.* 
על אחד שנים (נראה דקאי גם על מ"ש למעלה שהיה לו לומר להשיב מהר"ז) ולא דקדק המקרא במלתו:
rashi.eng: *twice as much.* Heb. למשנה, for one, two; and Scripture was not exact in its wording.

notes.2425: (tn): The Hebrew word קְשִׂיטָה (q�sitah) is generally understood to refer to a unit of money, but the value is unknown. The Hebrew word refers to a piece of silver, yet uncoined. It is the kind used in Gen 33:19 and Josh 24:32. It is what would be expected of a story set in the patriarchal age.
notes.2426: (sn): This gold ring was worn by women in the nose, or men and women in the ear.

rashi.heb:
*לפנים.* 
כל אשר היו אוהביו ומכיריו בטרם הגיעו אליו היסורים:
rashi.eng: *previous.* All who were his friends and acquaintances before the sufferings befell him.

rashi.heb:
*וינודו לו.* 
לשון קונפליינט"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and they bemoaned him.* Complaindre in Old French, to complain.

rashi.heb:
*קשיטה.* 
מעה:
rashi.eng: *one piece of money.* a ma’ah.

rashi.heb:
*ואיש.* 
וכל אחד ואחד (ר"ל שלא תאמר שהכונה שיש שנתנו לו קשיטה ויש שנתן לו נזם לכך כתב רש"י ואיש פירושו כל אחד ואחד מהר"ז):
rashi.eng: *and each one.* and every one of them.

rashi.heb:
*מראשיתו.* 
יותר מראשית עושרו:
rashi.eng: *more than his beginning.* More than his former wealth.

notes.2427: (tn): The word for “seven” is spelled in an unusual way. From this some have thought it means “twice seven,” or fourteen sons. Several commentators take this view; but it is probably not warranted.

rashi.heb:
*שבענה.* 
הם פעמים שבע שתי שביעיות כמו (ויקרא יב) שבועים שהם שתי שבועות:
rashi.eng: *fourteen.* Heb. שבענה. They were twice seven, two sevens, like (Lev. 12:5), שְׁבֻעַיִם which means two weeks.

notes.2430: (sn): The Hebrew name Keren-Happuch means “horn of eye-paint.”

rashi.heb:
*ויקרא שם האחת ימימה.* 
ע"ש יופיתן נקראו שמותיהן:
rashi.eng: *And he named the first Jemimah.* They were named according to their beauty.

rashi.heb:
*ימימה.* 
צחה ומלובנה כיום:
rashi.eng: *Jemimah.* Bright and white as the sun (יום).

rashi.heb:
*קציעה.* 
ריחה נודף ערב ומבושם כקציעה של בשם:
rashi.eng: *Keziah.* She had a fragrant and perfumed scent like the spice, cassia.

rashi.heb:
*קרן הפוך.* 
על שם הקרן שנותנין בו כחול ובורית שנאמר ותקרעי בפוך עיניך (ירמיהו ד׳:ל׳):
rashi.eng: *Keren-happuch.* Because of the horn in which they put stibium and lixivium, as it is stated (Jer. 4:30): “that you enlarge your eye with paint (בפוך).”

rashi.heb:
*ולא נמצא נשים יפות כבנות איוב וגו'.* 
ולא נמצא מעשה של נשים יפות כמעשה יופי של בנות איוב ומקרא זה דוגמת ויהי אנשים אשר היו טמאים (במדבר כ) וכן הרבה:
rashi.eng:
*Nowhere… were women as beautiful as Job’s daughters to be found.* 
An instance of beautiful women like the phenomenon of the beauty of Job’s daughters was not found. This verse is on the pattern of (Num. 9:6), “But there was [an incident of] men who were unclean.”

rashi.heb: *ויתן להם אביהם נחלה בתוך אחיהם.* מתוך חשיבותן ויפיין נתן להם נחלה עם האחים
rashi.eng: *And their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.* Because of (their esteem and) their beauty, he gave them an inheritance with their brothers.

notes.1: (sn): Psalm 1. In this wisdom psalm the author advises his audience to reject the lifestyle of the wicked and to be loyal to God. The psalmist contrasts the destiny of the wicked with that of the righteous, emphasizing that the wicked are eventually destroyed while the godly prosper under the Lord’s protective care.

rashi.heb:
*ושבע ימים.* 
מן שבע יאמר שבע בדבקות:
rashi.eng: *and sated with days.* Heb. וּשְׂבַע.From וְשָׂבֵעַ he says וּשְׂבַע, in the construct state.
